fields.lead: The field is mainly working on quantitative spatial models, why places diverge in opportunity and growth, and how trade, housing and transport costs shape where people and firms locate.

papers.title: Wages, Rents, and the Quality of Life
papers.why: Showed that wages and rents together reveal how much people value local amenities. The spatial-equilibrium logic underlies nearly all modern work on cities and regions.

papers.title: Increasing Returns and Economic Geography
papers.why: Showed how scale economies and transport costs can make activity cluster in a core-periphery pattern. It founded new economic geography, the basis of today's quantitative spatial models.

papers.title: Growth in Cities
papers.why: Found that city industries grow faster with diversity and competition than with specialization. The debate over which knowledge spillovers drive urban growth is still open.

papers.title: Measuring Economic Growth from Outer Space
papers.why: Showed night-lights from satellites can measure growth where official data are poor. Remote sensing is now a standard tool in spatial and development research.

papers.title: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States
papers.why: Found that Chinese import competition caused lasting job and wage losses in exposed US local labor markets. It changed how economists see the regional costs of trade.

papers.title: Where Is the Land of Opportunity? The Geography of Intergenerational Mobility in the United States
papers.why: Mapped large differences in upward mobility across US commuting zones. It made place central to the study of opportunity.

papers.title: Quantitative Spatial Economics
papers.why: Synthesized models that can be calibrated to real geographies to evaluate policies and shocks. It is the guide to the field's main modeling toolkit.

papers.title: The Revenge of the Places That Don't Matter (and What to Do About It)
papers.venue: Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society
papers.why: Linked populist votes to long-term decline in left-behind regions and argued for place-sensitive policy. It is central to the current debate on regional inequality and politics.

papers.title: Railroads of the Raj: Estimating the Impact of Transportation Infrastructure
papers.why: Showed that Indian railroads cut trade costs and raised real incomes, using a trade model to measure the effect. It set the template for evaluating infrastructure.

papers.title: Housing Constraints and Spatial Misallocation
papers.why: Argued that housing limits in productive cities like New York and San Francisco have substantially lowered US growth. It is central to the housing-supply debate.

more.title: From Managerialism to Entrepreneurialism: The Transformation in Urban Governance in Late Capitalism
more.venue: Geografiska Annaler: Series B, Human Geography
more.why: Described cities' turn to competing for capital through place-marketing and public-private deals. It remains the key critical-geography account of urban governance.

more.title: Buzz: Face-to-Face Contact and the Urban Economy
more.why: Argued that face-to-face contact is why high-skill activity stays concentrated in cities. The argument is now being tested by remote work.

more.title: Micro-Foundations of Urban Agglomeration Economies
more.venue: Handbook of Regional and Urban Economics, Vol. 4 (Elsevier)
more.why: Organized agglomeration benefits into sharing, matching and learning. The framework structures empirical work on why cities are productive.

more.title: Pre-colonial Ethnic Institutions and Contemporary African Development
more.why: Using night-lights and ethnic homeland maps, found pre-colonial political centralization predicts current development. It is a key piece of the institutions-and-geography debate.

more.title: Trade and the Topography of the Spatial Economy
more.why: Built a general-equilibrium model of trade over a continuous geography. It is a core building block of quantitative spatial models.

more.title: Local Economic Development, Agglomeration Economies, and the Big Push: 100 Years of Evidence from the Tennessee Valley Authority
more.why: Found the TVA's manufacturing gains persisted but national welfare gains were small. It is a central reference in the place-based policy debate.

more.title: The Economics of Density: Evidence from the Berlin Wall
more.why: Used Berlin's division and reunification to estimate agglomeration forces in a quantitative city model. It set the standard for within-city spatial models.

more.title: The Determinants and Welfare Implications of US Workers' Diverging Location Choices by Skill: 1980–2000
more.why: Showed that college workers sorted into high-wage, high-amenity cities, widening welfare inequality beyond wage gaps. It shapes work on spatial sorting.

more.title: The Impacts of Neighborhoods on Intergenerational Mobility I: Childhood Exposure Effects
more.why: Using movers, showed that each year in a better neighborhood raises children's adult outcomes. It made neighborhood effects causal and policy-relevant.

more.title: Regional Inequality in Europe: Evidence, Theory and Policy Implications
more.why: Documented diverging European regions and proposed policy by development type. It is the main reference for EU regional-policy debates.
